citations.quote: Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval containing $0$, let $B\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded open reference body with $C^1$ boundary, and let $U$ be an open neighborhood of $\overline B$. A material motion is a map $\chi\in C^2(I\times U;\mathbb R^3)$ whose slices $\chi_t(a)=\chi(t,a)$ are orientation-preserving $C^2$ diffeomorphisms onto their images, with $\chi(0,a)=a$. Its swept open region is $\Omega=\{(t,x):x\in\chi_t(U)\}$, its inverse label is $A(t,x)=\chi_t^{-1}(x)$, and its Eulerian velocity is $u(t,\chi(t,a))=\partial_t\chi(t,a)$. Set $L_{ij}=\partial_j u_i$, $D=(L+L^{\mathsf T})/2$, $\theta=\operatorname{tr}D=\operatorname{div}u$, and $D_t=\partial_t+u\cdot\nabla$. A branch is incompressible when $\theta=0$, so $D$ is symmetric and trace-free. Write $S:T=\operatorname{tr}(S^{\mathsf T}T)$ for the Frobenius contraction and $|S|=(S:S)^{1/2}$ for its norm. Define $\mathrm{Sym}_0(3)=\{D\in M_3(\mathbb R):D=D^{\mathsf T},\operatorname{tr}D=0\}$ and $\mathrm{Sym}^+(3)=\{C\in M_3(\mathbb R):C=C^{\mathsf T},z^{\mathsf T}Cz>0\text{ for every }z\ne0\}$. A rigid observer change is $x^*=Q(t)x+c(t)$ with $Q\in C^2(I,\mathrm{SO}(3))$, $c\in C^2(I,\mathbb R^3)$, and $\mathrm{SO}(3)=\{Q:Q^{\mathsf T}Q=I_3,\det Q=1\}$. A second-order tensor transforms as $S^*=QSQ^{\mathsf T}$; a constitutive response is objective when it obeys this rule at corresponding events.

For a generalized Newtonian branch, define

$$
\dot\gamma=(2D:D)^{1/2},\qquad \tau=2\eta(\dot\gamma)D,
$$

where $\eta:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ is finite and continuous.

Here $\tau_y$ is, by definition, the radius of the Frobenius stress ball at rest; other invariant normalizations require a corresponding parameter conversion. The graph is single-valued for $D\ne0$ and set-valued at rest.

Let $M_3(\mathbb R)=\mathbb R^{3\times3}$ be the real $3\times3$ matrices. For $M=(M_{ij})\in M_3(\mathbb R)$, define its trace by $\operatorname{tr}M=\sum_{i=1}^3M_{ii}$, and let $I_3$ be the $3\times3$ identity matrix, with diagonal entries $1$ and all other entries $0$.

Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval containing $0$, let $B\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded open reference body with $C^1$ boundary, and let $U$ be an open neighborhood of $\overline B$. A material motion is a map $\chi\in C^2(I\times U;\mathbb R^3)$ whose slices $\chi_t(a)=\chi(t,a)$ are orientation-preserving $C^2$ diffeomorphisms onto their images, with $\chi(0,a)=a$. Its swept open region is $\Omega=\{(t,x):x\in\chi_t(U)\}$, its inverse label is $A(t,x)=\chi_t^{-1}(x)$, and its Eulerian velocity is $u(t,\chi(t,a))=\partial_t\chi(t,a)$. Set $L_{ij}=\partial_j u_i$, $D=(L+L^{\mathsf T})/2$, $\theta=\operatorname{tr}D=\operatorname{div}u$, and $D_t=\partial_t+u\cdot\nabla$. A branch is incompressible when $\theta=0$, so $D$ is symmetric and trace-free. Write $S:T=\operatorname{tr}(S^{\mathsf T}T)$ for the Frobenius contraction and $|S|=(S:S)^{1/2}$ for its norm. Define $\mathrm{Sym}_0(3)=\{D\in M_3(\mathbb R):D=D^{\mathsf T},\operatorname{tr}D=0\}$ and $\mathrm{Sym}^+(3)=\{C\in M_3(\mathbb R):C=C^{\mathsf T},z^{\mathsf T}Cz>0\text{ for every }z\ne0\}$. A rigid observer change is $x^*=Q(t)x+c(t)$ with $Q\in C^2(I,\mathrm{SO}(3))$, $c\in C^2(I,\mathbb R^3)$, and $\mathrm{SO}(3)=\{Q:Q^{\mathsf T}Q=I_3,\det Q=1\}$. A second-order tensor transforms as $S^*=QSQ^{\mathsf T}$; a constitutive response is objective when it obeys this rule at corresponding events.

For the generalized Newtonian and Bingham branches, require $\theta=\operatorname{div}u=0$ throughout $\Omega$, so $D\in\mathrm{Sym}_0(3)$. In these branches, $\tau$ is a symmetric deviatoric extra stress, meaning $\operatorname{tr}\tau=0$; the total tension-positive Cauchy stress may additionally contain an isotropic pressure. In the conformation branch, $\tau_p$ and $\tau_s$ denote the polymer and solvent stresses separately and the pressure is a Lagrange multiplier. Stress is measured in Pa, $D$ and shear rate in $\mathrm{s}^{-1}$, viscosity in $\mathrm{Pa\,s}$, and a rate of stress power per volume in $\mathrm{W\,m^{-3}}$.

For a generalized Newtonian branch, define

$$
\dot\gamma=(2D:D)^{1/2},\qquad \tau=2\eta(\dot\gamma)D,
$$

where $\eta:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ is finite and continuous. Two permitted scalar choices are the Carreau form

$$
\eta_C(\dot\gamma)=\eta_\infty+(\eta_0-\eta_\infty)\bigl(1+(\lambda_C\dot\gamma)^2\bigr)^{(n_C-1)/2},
$$

with $\eta_0\ge\eta_\infty\ge0$ in $\mathrm{Pa\,s}$, $\lambda_C\ge0$ in seconds, and dimensionless $n_C>0$, and the regularized power form

$$
\eta_R(\dot\gamma)=m(\varepsilon^2+\dot\gamma^2)^{(n_R-1)/2},
$$

with $m>0$ in $\mathrm{Pa\,s}^{n_R}$, $\varepsilon>0$ in $\mathrm{s}^{-1}$, and dimensionless $n_R>0$. The unregularized power form $\eta_U=m\dot\gamma^{\,n_R-1}$ is defined only for $\dot\gamma>0$; its stress is extended by $\tau=0$ at $D=0$, so for $0<n_R<1$ the viscosity diverges at zero rate even though the extended stress can be continuous.

For the Bingham branch, let $\mu_p\ge0$ in $\mathrm{Pa\,s}$ and $\tau_y\ge0$ in $\mathrm{Pa}$. Adopt $\tau\in\mathcal B(D)$, where the set-valued graph on $\mathrm{Sym}_0(3)$ is

$$
\mathcal B(D)= \begin{cases} \{2\mu_pD+\tau_yD/|D|\},&D\ne0,\\ \{S\in\mathrm{Sym}_0(3):|S|\le\tau_y\},&D=0, \end{cases}
$$

where $\mathrm{Sym}_0(3)$ is the space of trace-free symmetric $3\times3$ real matrices. Here $\tau_y$ is, by definition, the radius of the Frobenius stress ball at rest; other invariant normalizations require a corresponding parameter conversion. The graph is single-valued for $D\ne0$ and set-valued at rest.

For an isothermal conformation branch, let $K=[t_0,t_1]\subset I$ be a compact interval with $t_0<t_1$. A pathline on $K$ is a continuously differentiable curve $x:K\to\mathbb R^3$ satisfying $(t,x(t))\in\Omega$ and $x'(t)=u(t,x(t))$ for every $t\in K$; derivatives at the endpoints are one-sided. Assume $\operatorname{div}u=0$ on $\Omega$ and take such a pathline. Let $C\in C^1(K;\mathrm{Sym}^+(3))$ be a dimensionless matrix-valued function. Along this pathline, the material derivative of $C$ is its ordinary derivative, $D_tC(t,x(t)):=\frac{d}{dt}C(t)$. Set $L(t)=\nabla u(t,x(t))$ and $D(t)=(L(t)+L(t)^{\mathsf T})/2$. Let $G>0$ be a modulus in Pa, $\lambda>0$ a relaxation time in seconds, $\eta_s\ge0$ a solvent viscosity in $\mathrm{Pa\,s}$, and $T_0>0$ a fixed temperature in K. Here an external thermostat is an idealized heat reservoir that maintains $T_0$ and accounts for heat released by this branch; it is an additional model assumption. Adopt

$$
\frac{dC}{dt}=LC+CL^{\mathsf T}-(C-I_3)/\lambda,\qquad \tau_p=G(C-I_3),\qquad \tau_s=2\eta_sD,\qquad w(C)=\frac G2\bigl(\operatorname{tr}C-\log\det C-3\bigr).
$$

The polymer and solvent stresses $\tau_p,\tau_s$ are measured in Pa, and $w$ is a stored-energy density in $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$. The determinant is positive because $C$ is symmetric positive definite. These are selected model equations on the stated smooth incompressible regime; they assert no empirical applicability to a particular material, fitted parameter values, PDE solution existence, or universal validity.

For any finite continuous viscosity $\eta:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ and the stress law $\tau=2\eta(\dot\gamma)D$, one has $\tau:D\ge0$. Under a $C^2$ rigid change of observer $x^*=Q(t)x+c(t)$, where $Q(t)\in SO(3)$, the transformed rate of strain is $D^*=QDQ^{\mathsf T}$, so the transformed stress is $\tau^*=Q\tau Q^{\mathsf T}$.

Then $\Phi$ is finite, nonnegative, and convex; $\mathcal B(D)=\partial\Phi(D)$ for every $D$; the graph is monotone in the sense that $(\tau_1-\tau_2):(D_1-D_2)\ge0$ whenever $\tau_i\in\mathcal B(D_i)$; every graph value satisfies $\tau:D\ge0$; and, for $Q\in SO(3)$, $\mathcal B(QDQ^{\mathsf T})=Q\mathcal B(D)Q^{\mathsf T}$.

Let $T>0$, let $J\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open interval containing $[0,T]$, let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open, and let $u\in C^1(J\times\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$ satisfy $\operatorname{div}u=0$ on a neighborhood of a $C^1$ trajectory $x:[0,T]\to\Omega$ with $x'(t)=u(t,x(t))$. Here $C^r$ means that coordinate partial derivatives through total order $r$ exist and are continuous. Set $L(t)=\nabla u(t,x(t))$ and $D(t)=(L(t)+L(t)^{\mathsf T})/2$, both with units $\mathrm{s}^{-1}$. Let $\mathrm{Sym}(3)$ denote the real symmetric $3\times3$ matrices and $\mathrm{Sym}^+(3)=\{M\in\mathrm{Sym}(3):v^{\mathsf T}Mv>0\text{ for every }v\ne0\}$. Let $C\in C^1([0,T];\mathrm{Sym}(3))$ be dimensionless and satisfy

$$
C'=LC+CL^{\mathsf T}-(C-I_3)/\lambda,\qquad C(0)=C_0\in\mathrm{Sym}^+(3),
$$

where $C_0\in\mathrm{Sym}^+(3)$, $I_3$ is the $3\times3$ identity matrix, $G>0$ is in $\mathrm{Pa}$, $\lambda>0$ is in $\mathrm{s}$, and $\eta_s\ge0$ is in $\mathrm{Pa\,s}$. Derivatives of $C$ at the endpoints are one-sided. Define $\tau_p=G(C-I_3)$ and $\tau_s=2\eta_sD$, both in $\mathrm{Pa}$. On $\mathrm{Sym}^+(3)$ define the stored-energy density $w(C)=\frac G2(\operatorname{tr}C-\log\det C-3)$ in $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$, where $\log r:=\int_1^r ds/s$ for $r>0$. Then $C(t)$ remains positive definite for every $t\in[0,T]$, $w(C(t))\ge0$, with equality exactly when $C(t)=I_3$, and for every $t$,

$$(\tau_s+\tau_p):D-\frac{d}{dt}w(C)=2\eta_sD:D+\frac{G}{2\lambda}\bigl(\operatorname{tr}C+\operatorname{tr}C^{-1}-6\bigr)\ge0.$$

For a $C^2$ rigid observer change $x^*=Q(t)x+c(t)$ with $Q(t)\in SO(3)$, set $C^*=QCQ^{\mathsf T}$ and $L^*=QLQ^{\mathsf T}+Q'Q^{\mathsf T}$. The conformation equation is covariant under this transformation, $D^*=QDQ^{\mathsf T}$, $\tau_p^*=Q\tau_pQ^{\mathsf T}$, $\tau_s^*=Q\tau_sQ^{\mathsf T}$, and $w(C^*)=w(C)$. Positivity is a forward-time conclusion from the initial time $0$; no backward-time positivity, PDE solution existence, or entropy-production claim is asserted.

For a $C^2$ rigid observer change $x^*=Q(t)x+c(t)$ with $Q(t)\in SO(3)$, set $C^*=QCQ^{\mathsf T}$ and $L^*=QLQ^{\mathsf T}+Q'Q^{\mathsf T}$. The conformation equation is covariant under this transformation, $D^*=QDQ^{\mathsf T}$, $\tau_p^*=Q\tau_pQ^{\mathsf T}$, $\tau_s^*=Q\tau_sQ^{\mathsf T}$, and $w(C^*)=w(C)$.

derivations.claim: In the generalized Newtonian branch, $\dot\gamma^2=2D:D$ and $\eta(\dot\gamma)\ge0$ by [F2], so $\tau:D=2\eta(\dot\gamma)D:D=\eta(\dot\gamma)\dot\gamma^2\ge0$. Under a rigid observer change, [F5] gives $D^*=QDQ^{\mathsf T}$ and $\tau^*=Q\tau Q^{\mathsf T}$; orthogonal conjugation preserves the Frobenius product, hence $\dot\gamma^*=\dot\gamma$. By the definition in [F1], the response is objective.

In the Bingham branch, when $D\ne0$, each allowed stress is $\tau=2\mu_pD+\tau_yD/|D|$, so $\tau:D=2\mu_p|D|^2+\tau_y|D|\ge0$. When $D=0$, every allowed stress has $\tau:D=0$; the graph value there is nonempty since it contains $0$, and for $D\ne0$ the graph value is a singleton. The kinematic identity $D^*=QDQ^{\mathsf T}$ in [F5] and the graph equivariance in [F6] give $\mathcal B(D^*)=Q\mathcal B(D)Q^{\mathsf T}$, so the graph response is objective, including at zero rate.

For the conformation branch, [F7] supplies positive definiteness and the exact identity in the Statement under its forward-time and regularity hypotheses; [F8] supplies objectivity. Set $A=C-I_3$. Since $C$ is positive definite, it is invertible and $C^{-1}$ is positive definite: for each nonzero $z$, $z^{\mathsf T}C^{-1}z=(C^{-1}z)^{\mathsf T}C(C^{-1}z)>0$. Matrix multiplication gives $AC^{-1}A=C+C^{-1}-2I_3$, so $\operatorname{tr}C+\operatorname{tr}C^{-1}-6=\operatorname{tr}(A^{\mathsf T}C^{-1}A)=\sum_{j=1}^3a_j^{\mathsf T}C^{-1}a_j\ge0$, where $a_j$ are the columns of $A$. Since $\eta_s\ge0$, the displayed stored-energy dissipation is nonnegative.

Steps 1.1–1.3 establish the conditional nonnegative mechanical or stored-energy dissipation and objectivity. Under the additional assumptions [A1], constancy of $T_0$ gives $\frac{d}{dt}w(C)=e_v'-T_0s_v'=(\tau_s+\tau_p):D-h-T_0s_v'$. Rearrangement yields $(\tau_s+\tau_p):D-\frac{d}{dt}w(C)=T_0(s_v'+h/T_0)=T_0\pi_s\ge0$ by step 1.3. Since $T_0>0$, $\pi_s\ge0$; no entropy conclusion is used or asserted without [A1].
